Now let's consider the vectors $\vvec=\twovec{-1}1$ and $\wvec=\twovec2{-2}$ as shown in [fig-span-linear-dep].

The vectors $\vvec$ and $\wvec$ and some linear combinations they create.

From the figure, we expect that $\bvec = \twovec02$ is not a linear combination of $\vvec$ and $\wvec$. Once again, we can verify this algebraically by constructing the linear system $$ \begin{bmatrix}\vvec \amp \wvec \end{bmatrix} ~ \xvec = \twovec02. $$ The augmented matrix has the reduced row echelon form $$ \left[ \begin{array}{rr|r} -1 \amp 2 \amp 0 \\ 1 \amp -2 \amp 2 \\ \end{array} \right] \sim \left[ \begin{array}{rr|r} 1 \amp -2 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array} \right], $$ from which we see that the system is inconsistent. Therefore, $\bvec=\twovec02$ is not in the span of $\vvec$ and $\wvec$.

We should expect this behavior from the coefficient matrix $$ \begin{bmatrix} -1 \amp 2 \\ 1 \amp -2 \\ \end{bmatrix} \sim \begin{bmatrix} 1 \amp -2 \\ 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{bmatrix}. $$ Because the second row of the coefficient matrix does not have a pivot position, it is possible for a linear system $\begin{bmatrix}\vvec \amp \wvec \end{bmatrix} ~\xvec = \bvec$ to have a pivot position in its rightmost column: $$ \left[ \begin{array}{rr|r} -1 \amp 2 \amp * \\ 1 \amp -2 \amp * \\ \end{array} \right] \sim \left[ \begin{array}{rr|r} 1 \amp -2 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 1 \\ \end{array} \right]. $$

If we notice that $\wvec = -2\vvec$, we see that any linear combination of $\vvec$ and $\wvec$, $$ c\vvec + d\wvec = c\vvec -2d\vvec = (c-2d)\vvec, $$ is actually a scalar multiple of $\vvec$. Therefore, the span of $\vvec$ and $\wvec$ is the line defined by the vector $\vvec$. Intuitively, this means that we can only walk to points on this line using these two vectors.
